intl_finance.document: Certification of Finances form (online; a notice and link appear in the Application Tracker). No bank statement or other financial documents are wanted with it. If admitted and enrolling, ISSS collects financial documents with the I-20 request: recent bank statement or letter, sponsor letter or approved loan letter, no more than 3 months old, liquid funds covering one year of expenses.

deadlines.label: Certification of Finances form
deadlines.note: Submit as soon as possible; the page says scholarship review begins in January. Page text was written for the previous cycle.

deadlines.label: Undergraduate New Student I-20 Request (ISSS)
deadlines.note: As soon as possible but no later than August 1 (year not stated; the page read was written for fall 2026 entry)

intl_finance.notes: The form is asked of applicants who are on or need a temporary visa; the page says it is not legally required, but without it the committee may be unable to finalize an admission decision or assess scholarship eligibility.

notes: Supplements 'none': the freshman checklist (source 1, which says the fall 2027 application launched Aug 1) lists Essay: 'Not required for admission' and no other written questions. Program-specific items (for example honors or music) were not researched. UMN's sites block automated requests, so pages were read from Internet Archive copies of the official URLs (source 1: 2026-08-20; source 2: 2026-04-22; source 3: 2026-05-11; source 4: 2026-05-11; source 5: 2026-09-11). The Certification of Finances page and the admitted-student checklist were written for the previous cycle (they mention scholarship letters by the end of March 2026 and the fall 2026 August 1 I-20 request date); 2026-27 dates were not confirmed. Source 4 gives the I-20 request step; source 5 gives the 3-month, liquid-funds document rules; source 2 confirms the Certification of Finances is part of the international freshman checklist.
